video_caption: The video features two men in a split-screen layout, both speaking into microphones. The man on the left wears a black baseball cap with white text "AWAKE" and a brown long-sleeve polo shirt, while the man on the right has short dark hair and is dressed in a light pink collared shirt. From 00:04 to 00:09, an image collage and an article headline are superimposed over the lower middle part of the screen. The collage shows two images of a man identified as Jackson Wang: one shirtless with blonde hair performing, and another with dark hair in a light green jacket. The article headline reads: "It's propaganda bulls***!' Hong Kong rapper Jackson Wang's emotional London concert tirade against anti-China media sparks flood of online support," followed by two bullet points summarizing the event. The background behind the left man features a neon sign that says "HOT POT BOYS DAVID & ANDREW," and behind the right man, a blue neon sign with an upward arrow above the words "UPSIDE MINDSET." Throughout the segment, both men actively speak and use hand gestures, with the right man appearing more animated and smiling frequently as they discuss the article and the celebrity. After 00:09, the image collage and article text disappear, focusing solely on the two speakers.

The video opens with a light-haired man, identified by Chinese text at the top left as Jackson Wang (王嘉尔) responding to rumors, on a concert stage wearing a sheer, black long-sleeved top and dark pants, holding a microphone and gesturing while singing and dancing. Chinese text at the top reads "王嘉尔在演唱会回应网传CCTV封杀 / 微博@韩饭桶" (Jackson Wang responds to online rumors of CCTV ban at concert / Weibo @HanFanTong) and at the bottom, "我很多时候对他们过度解读艺人艺术家的行为感到厌恶" (Many times I feel disgusted by their over-interpretation of artists' actions), translated as "like artists too much." He then says, "yo what do we do we sing we dance we do music that's it," matching the Chinese subtitle "我们在做什么呢 唱歌 跳舞 音乐 仅此而已" (What are we doing? Singing, dancing, music, that's it). The scene then transitions to a closer shot of the same man, now with light blue hair, holding a bottle and continuing to speak passionately, with a "SCMP" (South China Morning Post) logo in the top left. English subtitles display him saying, "there's so much f****** media talking about b*******, it's not like China. Media, f****** media." The video then cuts to a split-screen podcast setup featuring two men. The man on the left, wearing a black cap and a brown polo shirt, is speaking animatedly into a microphone, gesturing with his hands. The man on the right, wearing a pink jacket, listens and reacts. Overlaid on this scene are several YouTube comments from various users, some praising Jackson Wang for his statements ("takes guts and backbone," "brave to stand up and shout out for his own country"), and others suggesting he is "grinding the social credit points" or discussing media bias and freedom of speech related to China. The podcast hosts continue to discuss the reactions.

In a split-screen video, two East Asian men are engaged in a discussion, likely for a podcast or online show, each with a microphone. The man on the left wears a dark baseball cap with white text that reads "AWAKE" and a light brown long-sleeved polo shirt with a white collar. He is holding a black microphone close to his mouth, speaking animatedly, and occasionally gesturing with his hand. Behind him, a yellow neon sign displays "HOT POT BOYS DAVID & ANDREW" with a plant visible to his right. The man on the right, with short dark hair and bangs, wears a light pink collared jacket and has a black microphone in front of him. He listens with a slight smile and nod. Behind him is a blue neon sign that reads "UPSIDE MINDSET" with an upward-pointing arrow. During the left man's speech, a white rectangular text box appears on the screen displaying a Reddit comment: "tsu1028 5 days ago
Meanwhile buddy has tattoos that CCP won't even show on tv... wearing fishnet shirt which CCP definitely won't show on tv... nice try to get your social credit up
⬆️ 146" (The user 'tsu1028' posted this comment 5 days ago, implying that the person being discussed has tattoos and wears a fishnet shirt that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) would not permit on television, and that their actions are an attempt to gain social credit; it received 146 upvotes.) Later, as the man on the right reacts, another white text box appears, showing a different Reddit comment: "JEB 20 hours ago (edited)
be proud of your CHINESE heritage Jackson. Not everyone gets to say they have thousands of years of amazing culture and civilization that produced amazing philosophy/philosophers, foods, structure, instruments, art, music, etc... in their blood. Don't let these western media people make you feel ashamed for being unapologetically CHINESE!!!!" (The user 'JEB' posted this edited comment 20 hours ago, encouraging someone named Jackson to be proud of his Chinese heritage and rich cultural history, and to resist shame from Western media for being unapologetically Chinese.)

The video features a split screen, showing two Asian men speaking into microphones, likely for a podcast. On the left, a man wearing a black baseball cap and a light brown collared sweatshirt speaks animatedly, gesturing with his hand while holding the microphone. Behind him, a neon sign reads "HOT POT BOYS DAVID & ANDREW" with a green plant to its right. On the right, a man with short black hair and a light pink collared jacket smiles and looks towards the left, also holding a microphone. Behind him is a blue neon sign displaying "UPSIDE ASSET" with an upward-pointing arrow. At the bottom center, a comment bubble appears. Initially, a comment from "nnn" posted "3 minutes ago" states: "I think we should be worrying about his health and his alcoholism. It's obvious he's not okay and it feels like everyone is just ignoring it for some reason." (This comment addresses concerns about a person's health and potential alcoholism.) As the man on the left mentions "alcoholic" and compares it to Kanye, the comment remains on screen. Later, at 0:08, a different comment from "Lisette S." posted "2 days ago" replaces the first, accumulating "2.7K" likes. It reads: "Jackson is allowed to think good things about his country of heritage. Regardless of how we feel about its politics. Plus, are we all not aware of how harshly China treats its citizens and their families when they do criticize their country? They literally get their assets taken away in many cases. They tried to do it to Jackie Chan. Has no one in SK ever considered Jackson is just trying to protect himself and family?" (This comment defends Jackson's loyalty to his country, suggesting it might be for protection against harsh government actions rather than genuine political alignment.) The man on the right then starts to speak about people saying good things about their mother country.

The video displays a split-screen podcast or discussion featuring two Asian men. On the left, a man wearing a black baseball cap with "AWAKE" in white text and a brown collared sweatshirt speaks animatedly into a microphone, using hand gestures; behind him, a yellow neon sign reads "HOT POT BOYS DAVID & ANDREW" and a city skyline is visible through a window. On the right, another man with short dark hair, wearing a light pink collared shirt, listens and nods while holding a microphone; behind him, a blue neon sign reads "UPSIDE MINDSET". Text overlays appear below the speakers: first, a comment from "free loonaur" (2 days ago, edited) reads, "as a person from a country that's literally on the borderline of being fascist right now, I understand Jackson's points... people tend to forget that a country is not 100% its politics. it's also your family, friends, the places where you grew up in, language, culture, philosophy, art, etc etc. if you grew up/lived there, you probably have at least a couple things that you've grown to love about it. and you can refuse to support your country's political decisions while still continuing to be fond of a number of these things... Read more 90 Reply" (This comment supports the idea of distinguishing a country's culture/people from its politics). Later, another comment from "Tony Wu" (4 days ago) appears, stating, "he wants chinese $$$$$$$" (This comment suggests the speaker's views are motivated by financial gain related to China).
